evidence.claim: Catlow Rim grows from rolling hills at the valley’s north end into a cliff more than 1,000 feet above the floor at its southern end.
evidence.quote: At the north end of the valley, the rim begins as gentle rolling hills. The rim gets steeper and high as it runs south. At the south end of the valley, Catlow Rim has a cliff face that rises more than a 1,000 feet (300 m) above the valley floor.

evidence.claim: The basalt escarpment is the western face of the Steens Mountain fault block, along the valley’s eastern side.
evidence.quote: Catlow Rim is a prominent escarpment that forms the western face of the Steens Mountain fault block, overlooking the Catlow Valley. The rim is a basalt cliff that runs along the east side of the valley.

evidence.claim: The valley itself is a graben, a tectonic depression between the uplifted fault blocks of Hart Mountain and Steens Mountain.
evidence.quote: The Catlow Valley is a tectonic depression called a graben. It is bounded on the east and west by high, uplifted fault-block mountains—Hart Mountain to the west and Steens Mountain to the east
